title: Redwood POC weekly sync - cost econ
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost unit economics. Reviewed latest benchmark numbers (tokens/sec/$), caching savings observed with prefix/KV cache, and batching impacts on tail latency. Agreed to run a 24h full-traffic-ish benchmark, update cost model spreadsheet, and schedule infra deep-dive. Action items assigned.
next_steps: Redwood to share updated cost-model spreadsheet with per-route tokens/sec/$ assumptions (Alex)
Quantaco to provision representative traffic for 24h benchmark and provide sample prompts (Marta)
Schedule infra deep-dive to discuss VPC peering and KV cache sizing (Samir + Marta)
Check compliance docs and clarify data retention for logs (Jill + Priya)
action_items: Alex Moreno: send updated cost model + slides by 2026-08-21
Marta Ruiz: provide sample prompt set and traffic profile by 2026-08-24
Samir Patel: set up 24h benchmark run with Redwood infra by 2026-08-26
Jill Tan: share SOC2/ISO packet and retention answers by 2026-08-21
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-19 10:00am PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex (AE - Redwood), Samir (SE - Redwood), Jill (CSM), Ravi (Solutions Eng), Priya (PM - Quantaco), Leo (ML Eng), Marta (Infra), Tom (CTO)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick check, is the time still good?
[00:06] Priya: yep good here, thanks Alex.
[00:08] Leo: yup ready.
[00:10] Alex: awesome, so agenda for today  quick recap of last week's tuning, then the tokens per dollar numbers we ran overnight, some notes on caching and batching tradeoffs, and then next steps. Samir, you wanna kick off with the numbers?
[00:22] Samir: yeah sure, I'll share screen in a sec  so these are the aggregated run results from yesterday's 4-hour benchmark on dedicated g4dn-ish nodes, we tried three configs: baseline no-cache, prefix cache enabled, and prefix+KV cache. The headline:
[00:40] Samir: baseline achieved about 12k tokens/sec at tail but cost was about $0.045 per 1k tokens  that gives roughly 266k tokens per dollar, or inversely tokens/sec per dollar we compute as kind of tokens/sec/$ ~ (tokens/sec) / cost. It's messy but the sheet has the math.
[01:00] Priya: just to clarify, that baseline is with micro-batching size 8?
[01:05] Samir: yes micro-batch 8, dynamic batching enabled with a 50ms aggregation window.
[01:10] Leo: and model variant? 7B-quant1?
[01:13] Samir: correct, 7B q4_0 with kernel optimizations, not the 13B.
[01:17] Marta: okay and what latency numbers did you see at p95?
[01:20] Samir: baseline p95 around 420ms, p99 ~880ms. When we turned on prefix caching we saw tokens/sec jump to ~38k for repeated prefixes and cost drop ~35% effective on those routes. p95 improved to ~260ms, p99 ~560ms.
[01:40] Tom: wait so prefix cache only helps if you have repeated opening prompts?
[01:43] Samir: exactly, if your prompts have common prefixes  which I think you said in the doc you do for the assistant flows  then hit rates were 60-70% in our synthetic trace. But caveat: our synthetic trace might overestimate reuse.
[02:00] Priya: our real traffic has about 40% repeated prefixes, so expect smaller savings.
[02:06] Aless? (XX) [misc label glitch]
[02:10] Alex: haha, fireflies mis-label  ignore.
[02:12] Leo: the KV cache numbers?
[02:13] Samir: prefix + KV cache with 128MB KV per worker yielded tokens/sec ~29k across mixed traffic, cost effective drop of ~28% versus baseline. The KV cache helps mid-session reuse when users do iterative edits. But note memory and eviction tuning matter.
[02:30] Marta: how much extra memory are we talking? 128MB per worker adds up.
[02:33] Samir: yes it's additive; on our dedicated pool we had 8 workers per instance so that's ~1GB additional RAM across workers. For dedicated it's fine but on smaller instances you'd need to trade memory for fewer workers.
[02:48] Priya: can you remind us of the tokens/sec/$ changes summarized?
[02:51] Samir: sure  baseline ~266k tokens/$, prefix-cache during high-hit routes ~420k tokens/$, mixed traffic with prefix+KV ~340k tokens/$. Those numbers fold in observed hit rates from the test.
[03:07] Leo: that aligns with our internal expectation; but what about batching tradeoffs? we worry about latency tails if we increase batch size.
[03:15] Samir: good question  we ran batch sizes 8, 16 and 32. Throughput improves roughly linearly up to 16, then diminishing returns. However p99 jumps with batch 32 for single-request latency  p99 increased to ~1.6s. So for customer-facing low-latency flows we recommend max batch 16 with dynamic early flush for urgent requests.
[03:38] Alex: and that's a per-route knob in Redwood routing?
[03:40] Ravi: yep you can set per-route SLOs and batching profiles, and have fallback to a lower-latency pool for priority requests.
[03:47] Tom: what's the cost delta if we do two pools (low-latency small batch + high-throughput batched)?
[03:51] Samir: approximate  running 60% traffic on high-throughput pool and 40% on low-latency increases cost ~18% compared to single mixed pool but gives p99 under 700ms for the priority pool. We modeled it in the sheet.
[04:05] Priya: any tradeoffs with quantization? we saw some output quality delta on q4 variants.
[04:11] Samir: yes quantization tradeoffs. q4_0 was fine for most regen prompts but for few-shot code generation we did see hallucination increases in our evals. Option: use 7B fp16 for sensitive routes and q4 for others  price delta about 30-40% higher for fp16.
[04:28] Leo: hmm for our code-assist feature we need higher fidelity  probably not q4 there.
[04:32] Alex: makes sense to pin that route to fp16 variant and use higher batch sizes on other routes.
[04:36] Marta: what's the recommended KV sizing policy? 128MB looked good here but will eviction cause flakiness?
[04:41] Samir: eviction policy LRU with per-session TTL 30 mins in our test. If your sessions are longer we can increase or sharded KV. Also you can persist warm keys to a hot store to pre-warm workers. But that introduces infra complexity.
[04:55] Priya: ok noted.
[04:57] [05:00] Jill: quick compliance check  for the benchmark logs we store, what's the retention and are tokens persisted?
[05:05] Samir: benchmark logs can be stored in customer-controlled S3 for private deployments; hosted collects anonymized usage. We do not store raw prompt text unless enabled, and you can enable KMS encryption. I can send the SOC2/ISO packet after the call.
[05:18] Jill: great. Priya, does that meet your bar or do you need additional legal review?
[05:23] Priya: we'll need legal confirmation but looks okay for the pilot.
[05:25] Tom: I'd like to understand price per 1M tokens for planning spreadsheets, can you give an estimate?
[05:30] Samir: rough numbers from the sheet  baseline ~ $170 per 1M tokens, with prefix-high-hit routes ~ $102 per 1M, mixed prefix+KV ~ $125 per 1M. Again these assume our infra and the model variant.
[05:45] Leo: that baseline feels higher than our on-prem runs, are we comparing apples to apples?
[05:50] Samir: good point  our hosted config includes node overhead, multi-tenant bookkeeping, and higher p95 SLOs. If you self-host the dedicated pool or private deployment you could reduce that unit cost by ~15-25% depending on instance discounts.
[06:06] Priya: what about burst capacity? we have spiky traffic.
[06:09] Ravi: Redwood has burst capacity options; you can reserve a base pool and allow burst to a shared pool with throttles. That lowers committed cost but you may see increased latencies during extreme bursts.
[06:21] Marta: for the 24h benchmark, do we need to mirror traffic exactly?
[06:24] Samir: ideally yes  provide a replayable trace with timestamps and sample prompts. If you can anonymize them, that's fine. We'll run the run-for-24h and produce per-route tokens/sec/$ and hit rates.
[06:36] Priya: we'll put that together; Marta will take point.
[06:39] Marta: will do.
[06:41] Alex: ok, recap of next steps  Alex will send the updated cost-model, Samir will coordinate the 24h run once Marta shares trace, Jill will send compliance docs, and we'll have infra deep-dive next week. Any blockers?
[06:54] Tom: just legal signoff timeline, but nothing blocking technical progress.
[06:58] Priya: sounds good.
[07:00] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the sheet.
[07:05] [END]
